bodies.name: Barnard d
bodies.description: A small planet found by radial velocity (minimum mass well below Earth's); probably rocky. Too hot for liquid water.

orbit.note: Drawn circular: the fitted eccentricities (d 0.04, b 0.03, c 0.08, e 0.04; Basant et al. 2025 via the NASA Exoplanet Archive) are consistent with zero within 2σ. A circular drawing can misplace the planet along its orbit by up to 2e rad (3–9°); the phase arc does not include that. Orbit inclination unknown (radial-velocity detection). Phase: the planet is drawn in front of the star (on the 'toward Earth' arrow) at t0 = BJD 2460243.70 +0.08/−0.07 (Basant et al. 2025, Table 3), read as the time of inferior conjunction as used by juliet/RadVel (tc); the paper text says periastron. 1-sigma phase spread from t0 and P (2.3402 ± 0.0003 d): ±16° on 2025-04-24, ±25° on 2026-10-05 (linear propagation; the t0-P covariance is not published and is ignored). The sense of motion on the sky is unknown: drawn counter-clockwise seen from above.

facts.label: Orbital period
facts.source: Basant et al. 2025, ApJL 982, L1, Table 3 (arXiv:2503.08095)

facts.label: Reference time t0
facts.source: Basant et al. 2025, ApJL 982, L1, Table 3 (arXiv:2503.08095), listed as BJD − 2450000. Verified for the value only: the paper calls t0 the time of periastron, the fitting code (juliet, RadVel 'tc') the time of conjunction; see the orbit note

representation_note: 3D model drawn from published catalog and literature values, not measured by SPHEREx unless a fact says 'seen by SPHEREx' (each fact shows its source) - not an image. What no source gives is not drawn: an unknown temperature is drawn grey and an unknown size at a fixed marker size, not to scale. Sizes and distances may be exaggerated for visibility.

notes: Values checked on 2026-11-14 against the NASA Exoplanet Archive, SIMBAD (CfA mirror), Gaia DR3, VizieR and the cited papers (tasks/WS7-3d-systems.md, WS7-2). Facts still marked 'unverified' are estimates no source states. The 'seen by SPHEREx' facts were copied from the validation records (docs/validation/; AI analysis with an independent second analysis; the five records were human-reviewed on 2026-11-15, a guided review that did not re-run the analyses), not from that catalog cross-check.

Planet phases follow the t0 and periods of Basant et al. 2025 (Table 3), read as times of inferior conjunction: a position on a real date is a prediction with the 1-sigma spread given in each orbit note. The star's rotational phase is not known.
Planet masses are minimum masses (M sin i) and planet radii are estimates: radial velocity measures neither the inclination nor the size.
